claim: Note 3 sends readers to Ch. 14 §1.6 for the hybrid NP in There was no stopping her. Page 333 cites the same section for the argument that gerund-participials are clauses.
evidence_summary: Ch. 14 begins §1.5 on p. 1187 and §1.6 on p. 1191. The hybrid constructions are on p. 1189 [57], and the argument for the clausal analysis runs through pp. 1188–1190.
finding: Both references should point to §1.5. Section 1.6 concerns the case of the subject. Ch. 16, p. 1394, repeats the same reference.
inference: Do the references lead to the passages they cite?

evidence.passage: §2, p. 332 n. 3 and p. 333. Both cite Ch. 14, §1.6.
evidence.example: Ch. 14 contents, p. 1171: “1.5 The structure of gerund-participials 1187”, “1.6 Case of the subject NP in gerund-participials 1191”. Page 1189 has “(b) Hybrid constructions” with [57ii b] There’ll be no stopping her.
evidence.establishes: The cited section begins after the material it is cited for.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
